design.approach: Three-phased intake generalization inside csm-orchestrate, executed in a wt-session worktree with serial per-task commits. Phase 1: a typed csm-orchestrate-request/1 envelope (kind enum over the skill taxonomy verbs, prompt, artifactRef, goalSlug, constraints, requestedSignals) added under csm-orchestrate/schemas/ and registered in schemas/registry.json; lib/intake.mjs switches on schema marker to resolve approach/plan/request kinds and fails closed with a router hint otherwise. Phase 2: lib/request-router.mjs classifyRequest maps a request to {goalSlug, kind, routes, signals} using the 13 skills' activation boundaries as the routing table; explicit-mode skills receive explicit signals only (no heuristic widening); request->plan/intent chaining stays manual per activation boundaries. Phase 3: the DRIVER (scripts/run-orchestrator.mjs + scripts/lib/agent-session-executor.mjs) wires a csm-build executor binding whose execute() spawns a wt-session csm-build agent session (wt-session create <slug>, prompt file with the plan path and csm-build activation text, '<agent-cli> run --prompt-file' inside the worktree) and awaits the typed child result (csm-build-output/1 written by the build session); spawn is env-gated and hermetic tests stub the child binary; when gated off, the default blocked agent-session-required result is unchanged. orchestrate() lib itself gains no process runtime: the injected executor stays the only execution authority (contract preserved). Approach/1 intake path is untouched code-wise (intake.mjs routes it to the existing loadApproach/compileApproach flow) so parity holds.
